name: repo-identity-guard
description: Know instantly whether it's safe to work, commit, push, or let an AI agent run commands in this repo.

repoIdentityGuard.profiles.description: Profiles (e.g. Work, Personal) matched against a repo's remote owner to determine the expected identity and rules.

id.description: Stable unique identifier for this profile.

label.description: Short display label, for example Work or Personal.

gitName.description: Expected Git commit author name for matching repositories.

gitEmail.description: Expected Git commit author email for matching repositories.

expectedRemoteOwners.description: GitHub owners/orgs (wildcards allowed) whose repos should match this profile.

expectedBranchPatterns.description: Wildcard branch name patterns considered normal for this profile, e.g. feature/*.

strictPushSetup.description: When true, HTTPS remotes and generic SSH hosts are treated as Not Safe until locked to this profile.

trustedSshHostAliases.description: SSH host aliases (e.g. github-work, from a ~/.ssh/config Host entry) this profile explicitly trusts as an approved push route. A custom SSH alias is never trusted just for being non-generic — only aliases listed here can make Push Account read as a trusted route, and even then it is never cryptographic proof of the remote account.

repoIdentityGuard.protectedBranches.description: Local branch policy: branch names Repo Identity Guard treats as protected on this machine. Not synced with GitHub's own branch protection settings.

repoIdentityGuard.requireLocalIdentity.description: Require matched repositories to set the expected identity in local Git config, even when the effective identity currently matches via global config.

repoIdentityGuard.includeMemoryInAiConte.description: Off by default. When enabled, your pinned Repo Memory note is included in 'Copy Context for AI'. Pinned notes are free text you wrote for yourself and may contain sensitive info — only enable this if you're sure.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Read-only repo scanning still runs in untrusted workspaces. Fixing commit identity and running saved commands are blocked until the workspace is trusted.
